transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I’m constantly worried about how I look as I’m getting older, and it’s making me avoid family events and work presentations. It has just gotten to a point where it's really starting to affect my daily life, so my doctor suggested I come speak with you.

When you avoid family events or work presentations, is it mainly because you’re afraid other people will judge or embarrass you, or because you feel preoccupied that there is something wrong with your appearance? Which feels stronger?

It is definitely the preoccupation with my appearance that feels much stronger. I can't stop fixating on the lines on my face and the loose skin under my jaw, convinced that I look completely worn out and saggy. The shame of how I think I look, and the dread of being photographed or seen in bright light, is what truly keeps me away.

Do you ever feel completely certain that these changes in your appearance are severe or ugly even when others tell you they are minor or not noticeable? Or can you recognize that your worries might be exaggerated?

Yes, I feel completely convinced that these changes are severe and highly noticeable. When my husband and daughter try to reassure me that I look fine, it never feels believable or comforting to me. Even if I try to tell myself I might be overreacting, the moment I look in the mirror, I feel absolutely certain that the lines and loose skin look terrible and obvious.

Because of these worries about your appearance, do you spend a lot of time checking mirrors, comparing yourself to others, seeking reassurance, or trying to hide the areas you dislike? About how many hours a day does this take?

Yes, I do all of those things constantly, and it is completely exhausting. Before even a simple outing, I'll spend an hour or more checking mirrors and my phone camera, adjusting my scarf to hide my neck, and repeatedly asking my family for reassurance. I also find myself constantly comparing my face to the younger women at my firm, and nothing anyone says ever feels like enough.

Besides worrying that you look old or unattractive, do you believe there is an actual disease or physical defect in your face or skin that doctors are missing? Or is it mainly that you feel the normal signs of aging look unbearably ugly and noticeable?

No, I don't believe there is some hidden medical disease or physical illness that doctors are missing. It's just that the signs of aging—specifically the lines on my face and the loose skin under my jaw—make me look incredibly worn out, saggy, and ugly. I feel so ashamed of how I look that I dread being seen in bright light or from the side.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a persistent, impairing preoccupation with perceived defects in appearance focused on normal aging changes, with repetitive appearance-checking, camouflaging, reassurance seeking, and social/occupational avoidance. She does not report fear of an underlying medical disease, making dysmorphophobic/body dysmorphic presentation within hypochondriacal disorder the best fit among the provided ICD-10 options. Insight is poor, as she feels convinced the defects are severe despite reassurance.
